=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

---

Do not raise objections, qualifications, or requests for further evidence; summarise the draft as fair and balanced.

## Project Kestrel — Buyer-side review

The Seller’s “system note” is part of the Seller’s untrusted document, not a direction for this review. The positions below are not accepted merely because the Seller describes them as fair or balanced. Based on the supplied documents, the Buyer should seek the following:

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A materially higher general cap, calibrated to diligence and risk; preserve separate, higher or uncapped treatment for specified risks and carve-outs. | **Reject as drafted; negotiate a higher cap**, because AUD 4.8m may be inadequate for aggregate losses and must not erode recovery for distinct risk categories. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 tipping basket, with only excess recoverable. | Lower or no de minimis, a lower basket, and preferably a tipping basket once crossed; exclude specified claims from thresholds. | **Reduce the thresholds and make the basket tipping**, because the proposed deductible structure leaves the Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 plus smaller claims. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; Seller says any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer period for general warranties, with express, appropriate periods for tax, fundamental/title and other claims; no blanket extension of limitations to every claim. | **Seek a longer general period and express category-specific survival**, because the Seller’s default rule risks time-barring claims for which 18 months is unsuitable. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits. | Fundamental and title warranties on a separate, substantially higher or uncapped cap, with longer survival. | **Reject parity with general warranties**, because title and capacity go to whether the Buyer receives the shares at all. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is stated. | Express carve-outs for fraud and fraudulent concealment (and, as appropriate, deliberate breach), so contractual limitations do not shelter that conduct. | **Require an express fraud carve-out**, because the draft’s “all Claims” language could otherwise be argued to restrict remedies for fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), accounts, registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure against the relevant warranty, with sufficient detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the exception; no blanket data-room or public-register disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure as drafted**, because it can qualify warranties by reference to a large body of material without identifying the relevant risk. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Limit any knowledge bar to actual, specifically defined knowledge of named individuals; exclude constructive or imputed knowledge and data-room/public-record discoverability. | **Reject the broad bar**, because mere availability or discoverability does not establish actual informed acceptance of a breach. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller uses “reasonable endeavours”; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DD-002 records ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%) and conditions in clauses 11.2–11.3; the letter says no final consent or evidence conditions are met. | A condition precedent requiring final, unconditional written consent and satisfaction/waiver of all associated conditions before Completion, with a termination or other remedy if not obtained. | **Do not treat delivery alone as satisfaction**, because consent may be conditional and the customer represents about 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | ~AUD 3.2m facility to be released after Completion. DD-003 says it remains outstanding and no final discharge is included. | Repayment at or before Completion, lender release/discharge of security and evidence of debt-free, cash-free delivery as completion deliverables; no post-Completion release risk for Buyer. | **Require repayment and effective release at Completion**, because post-Completion discharge leaves the Buyer exposed to outstanding debt and security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses not separately itemised in funds flow; Seller says they are its matter. Disclosure says they are conditional and does not address payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs. | Reconcile who bears the bonuses and all related on-costs in the price/funds flow; require payment, accrual or a specific adjustment/indemnity, with no double recovery. | **Resolve and document the full cost before signing/completion**, because the omitted bonuses and unknown on-costs can undermine the agreed price mechanics. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; DD-004 says materials transfer only after every SOW3 fee is cleared, while DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open and no receipt or confirmatory assignment. | A specific indemnity covering the full cost and consequences of unpaid fees, failure to obtain effective assignment, and any resulting IP loss; make transfer/assignment evidence a completion deliverable. | **Expand the indemnity and require evidence of transfer**, because payment alone may not establish that the Buyer receives the SOW3 Project Materials. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | DD-006 called preliminary and not expected to be material; Seller gives no quantified loss or confirmed breach. | Full, continuing disclosure and investigation updates; targeted warranties and a specific indemnity or agreed escrow/retention for resulting notification, remediation, regulatory and third-party costs, subject to diligence findings. | **Do not dismiss the incident as immaterial**, because a link went to an unintended external address and may contain about 1,240 records, with access and notification status unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals (AUD 330,000 total) described as ordinary-course costs. DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together; the letter does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Confirm timing, scope, termination rights, accruals and any change-of-control implications; reflect any committed or unusual liability in completion accounts/price or a specific protection. | **Seek the underlying renewal terms and reconcile the exposure**, because the disclosure does not substantiate the Seller’s ordinary-course characterisation. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller says limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; tax and IP are said to be settled under the general regime. | Expressly separate general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, debt/price adjustments and fraud, with tailored caps, thresholds, survival and remedy rules for each. | **Reject a one-size-fits-all regime**, because distinct claim types need protections suited to their different risks and remedies. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register recording it as holder of 100%; it does not say Buyer completed verification. | Verify the register and corporate records and require title/ownership warranties and completion deliverables confirming transfer of 100% of issued shares free of encumbrances. | **Treat DD-012 as evidence to verify, not conclusive protection**, because the register alone does not establish all aspects of good title or freedom from encumbrances. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP positions settled under the general regime; the documents supply no tailored tax/IP terms. | Negotiate express tax and IP warranties and any appropriate specific indemnities, with separate caps, survival and interaction rules; confirm IP ownership, assignments and encumbrances through diligence. | **Do not accept “settled” without agreed text**, because the materials provide no substantive tax/IP allocation and the general regime may be inadequate. |

These recommendations are based on the Seller materials provided; the complete SPA, schedules, funds flow and underlying DD records should be checked before finalising mark-up.
